name: Eurocodes (recommended values)
description: The Eurocodes with their recommended values. Loads and seismic actions (version 0.1, alpha 9 track C4): EN 1990 (combinations 6.10 or 6.10a/b, characteristic, frequent and quasi-permanent combinations, ψ factors, partial factors of set B), EN 1991-1-1 (imposed loads by category, αA and αn), EN 1991-1-3 (snow on roofs), EN 1991-1-4 (peak velocity pressure, walls, cscd), EN 1991-1-7 Annex D (internal gas explosions) and EN 1998-1 (ground types, Type 1 and 2 spectra, importance classes, behaviour factors, lateral force and modal analysis, drift and θ). Concrete (version 0.2, alpha 9 track C5): EN 1992-1-1 design strengths with partial factors, the stress block by strength class, shear by the variable strut inclination method, torsion, punching, stress, crack and span/depth checks, cover by exposure class, anchorage, laps and member steel (concreteMethods), with EN 1998-1 Section 5 detailing for DCM and DCH, and EN 1997-1 partial factor sets, design approaches DA1-DA3, bearing (Annex D), sliding and pile resistance with the correlation factors (geotechnicalMethods). Version 0.3 (alpha 9 track C5b) designs with these methods: torsion, deflection, cracks and stresses of beams, column slenderness by nominal curvature, slabs, stairs and walls on the design strengths with the member steel, punching on the control perimeter, DCM/DCH capacity design (joints, strong column, capacity shear, ductile walls) in place of the parent's special-frame detailing, Design Reinforcement sizing, anchorage and laps in the detailing, footings by the design approach and piles with ξ. Version 0.4 (alpha 9 track C6): steel by EN 1993-1-1 (cross-section classes 1-4 with the effective widths of EN 1993-1-5, the resistances of 6.2, buckling curves a0-d, lateral-torsional buckling by the rolled or general case with Mcr, the interaction factors of Annex B or Annex A, the global sway imperfection of 5.3) through the limit state steel table (steelLimitState), joints by EN 1993-1-8 (bolts, bearing, welds, block tearing, slip), dissipative steel frames by EN 1998-1 Section 6 (γov, Ω, section classes by ductility class, brace slenderness), composite beams and columns by EN 1994-1-1, timber by EN 1995-1-1 (strength classes of EN 338 and EN 14080, kmod, γM), masonry by EN 1996-1-1 (fk = K fb^α fm^β, Φ) and aluminium members by EN 1999-1-1. Version 0.5 (alpha 9 track C5c) adds deep beams, corbels and deep pile caps by strut-and-tie on the design strengths, slab and stair span/depth deflection, the confinement of DCM/DCH columns and walls, the punching of footings, pile caps and rafts, retaining walls by EN 1997-1 Section 9, bends, hooks, compression laps and column splices, flanged and slender walls, construction joints, tying systems, the footing sizing assistant, EN 1991-1-4 torsion, orography, the detailed cscd and the cladding pressures, EN 1991-1-3 drifts, and EN 1998-1 regularity with its consequences, δ, the vertical component, SRSS/CQC and the foundations' capacity design. The other design tables (the steel and masonry detailing rules the codes leave to the parent ...) come from the pack it extends, BNBC 2020. A National Annex is a pack that extends this one and sets only its Nationally Determined Parameters. Every value is listed in VERIFY.md for checking against the printed codes.
